title: What to Do with a Remainder
short: Drop it, round up or report it, depending on the question.
trouble: Children answer "8 R2 buses" or round down when the extra people still need a seat.

blocks.html: A remainder is a real amount: people, inches, dollars. After you divide, read the question again and decide what the remainder means.

There are three common cases. Round up when the leftovers still need something (one more van). Drop it when the leftovers cannot make a whole one (a piece too short to use). Report it when the question asks what is left over.

The quotient counts full groups. In "30 people, 7 per van," $30 \div 7 = 4$ R 2: four vans are full and 2 people are still waiting. They need a van too, so the answer is 5. The math is the same each time; the story decides the answer.

blocks.name: g4-groups
blocks.cap: 30 people in vans of 7: 4 full vans and 2 people left. Those 2 still need a ride.

blocks.title: Round up
blocks.q: 30 people go on a trip. Each van holds 7. How many vans are needed?
steps: The 2 extra people need a seat, so add a van.

blocks.title: Drop the remainder
blocks.q: A ribbon is 46 inches long. How many 6-inch pieces can you cut?
steps: The 4 inches left is too short for another piece.

blocks.title: The remainder is the answer
blocks.q: 29 cookies are shared equally by 4 friends, as many as possible each. How many are left over?
steps: Each friend gets 7, and the question asks what is left.

blocks.html: Answering "4 R 2 vans" or "4 vans." A number with an R is not an answer to "how many vans?", and 4 vans leaves 2 people behind. Picture the story and ask: what happens to the leftovers?
